decisions.text: type bar: categories compared by value
the 2025 target of each category drawn as a flat mark across its bar, named once (R11-4, G8.13, G5.5)
the 5% over target of each category drawn as a flat mark across its bar, named once (R11-4, G8.13, G5.5)
nominal categories sorted by value, descending (by series use)
2025 target, a reference, as a flat marker across each bar of 2025 use, in the strong shade of the bar's hue, on the bars' zero-based scale (G1.60, G7.57)
5% over target, a second reference, as a dotted mark across each bar in the dark grey, the look of a reference line, so that it stays apart from the first's solid mark (SPEC §6.12.2)
“Data Centre” and “Chemistry Building” come within 10 pt of each other under vertical bars, with every multi-word name wrapped: horizontal bars, names right-aligned at the left
labels as a set, 0 decimals, bare numbers: 0, 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000
a horizontal scale: bare numbers, and its title centred below with the unit in parentheses: “Electricity used in 2025 (MWh)”
a legend above the plot, below the title: the names do not fit beside the first bar (G5.7, G5.10, D-7)
legend entries in series order: 2025 use, 2025 target, 5% over target (G5.8)
the title wraps onto two lines

findings.message: the marks of 2025 target and 5% over target lie too near to be told apart on Castle Court Halls, Arts Tower and Students' Union: the scale is too coarse for the distance between them; a deviation from 2025 target (transform) shows it
findings.title: a reference per bar as a short flat mark across it, labelled once

source.shows: two references across each bar: the target a solid mark in the dark grey, the threshold a dotted one, named once beside the first bar; at this scale the two lie a few points apart, which the report warns of (R11-4: a deviation shows the distance)
